response.title: can a solar generator power a deep freezer
response.answer:
Yes! A solar generator can power a deep freezer, including a chest freezer or upright freezer. The key is choosing a generator with enough battery capacity (Wh) and output power (W).

How big of a solar generator do you need?

Most modern deep freezers use approximately 50–200 watts while their compressors are running, but they cycle on and off throughout the day.

Solar generator battery

	

Estimated freezer runtime




500 Wh

	

5–10 hours




1,000 Wh

	

10–20 hours




2,000 Wh

	

20–40 hours




3,000 Wh

	

30–60 hours




5,000 Wh

	

2–4 days

Estimates assume approximately 100–200 watts of average daily energy use per hour of operation (roughly 1.2–2.4 kWh/day), with inverter losses. Actual runtime depends heavily on freezer efficiency, temperature, and usage.

What specifications should you look for?

Battery capacity: At least 1,000–2,000 Wh for useful backup time.

AC output: Preferably 1,000 W or higher to handle compressor startup surges.

Pure sine wave inverter: Recommended for freezer compressors.

Solar input: 200–400 W of solar panels can help recharge the battery during daylight, depending on weather and energy consumption.

Can it run continuously with solar panels?

Yes, potentially. If your solar panels generate enough electricity each day to replace what the freezer consumes, you could run it indefinitely under favorable sunlight conditions.

For example, a freezer consuming 1 kWh per day might need approximately 300–400 W of solar panels, plus enough battery storage to cover nighttime and cloudy weather.

        <radio value="24 hours">24 hours</radio>
        <radio value="3 days">3 days</radio>
        <radio value="continuously">Continuously</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Will you have solar panels connected?</label>
      <radio-group direction="row" value={solar} onChange={setSolar}>
        <radio value="yes">Yes</radio>
        <radio value="no">No</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate recommended generator size <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
